facts.text: The user-facing driver object is the class smu
The README calls the modconsmu folder an importable pure-Python driver that uses pyusb
The constructor finds the instrument by USB vendor id 0x6666 and product id 0x0005
The constructor reads the DAC, VADC, IADC and RES calibration words with four vendor control transfers and converts them into the gain and shunt values
The constructor registers set(amps=0) with atexit as its safety feature
update() writes the DAC target with the UPDATE vendor request, reads 12 bytes and returns the measured voltage, measured current and modVolt; its docstring says it returns actual V/I
update() maps a voltage target to the 12-bit code zeroV - v/scaleFactorV and a current target to zeroI + i*10000
set(volts, amps) stores one target, switches between voltage and current driving and calls update(); it raises NotImplementedError when both are given
The firmware UPDATE handler writes both DAC bytes and returns four ADC result pairs, the timer bytes and a 12-byte reply
The firmware defines the vendor requests UPDATE 1, SET_DIGOUT 2, GET_DAC_VALS 3, SET_DAC_VALS 4, GET_VADC_VALS 5, GET_IADC_VALS 7, GET_RES_VAL 9, GET_NAME 11 and SET_NAME 12
The example charger sets a constant current with set(amps=...), switches to a constant voltage with set(volts=...), and disables charging with set(amps=0)
The constructor's maxV=9.93 and minV=-10.45 are the ends of the voltage conversion scale and are used only to derive scaleFactorV
